Relevant Tertiary qualifications in Business, Commerce, Hospitality, Hotel Management or equivalent experience.

Demonstrated effective interpersonal and written communication skills with a high level of organisations skills and the ability to effectively manage and prioritise work loads.

Participants may also have opportunities to engage with clinical dermatology services, attend educational meetings and contribute to quality improvement initiatives.

Monash Health is Victoria's largest and most comprehensive health service. For more than 170 years, Monash Health and its predecessors have provided safe, high-quality healthcare for people at every life stage. With 25,500 employees, we provide care to south-eastern metropolitan Melbourne and rural Victoria from over 40 locations, via telehealth, within local communities and in people's homes.


We recognise the value of equal employment opportunity. We are committed to patient safety, promoting fairness, equity and diversity in the workplace and to Child Safe Standards. At Monash Health we are relentless in our pursuit of excellence and work to our six guiding principles and our five ICare values.



About Monash Doctors 


To help grow your career, there are more than 1,900 Junior and 1,700 Senior Doctors at Monash Health in over 200 medical specialties. We offer unparallel opportunities in Victoria's largest & most clinically diverse teaching health service. 




About Monash Anaesthesia






Providing anaesthetic support to 8 Monash Health facilities, Monash Health currently employs over 150 Specialist Anaesthetists and supports the Monash-Southern Anaesthetic training program, with close to 100 trainees. We cover an extensive range of tertiary surgical disciplines.






Monash Health is looking for Consultant Anaesthetists to work within Monash Health alongside other anaesthetists working at Dandenong and Cranbourne ICC, Casey, Clayton, Moorabbin and Monash Children's and the Victoria Heart hospitals.






A significant EFT is available, with a combination of Fractional and Full time positions, with the positions requiring a minimum commitment to Monash Health of 20 hours per week.












About The Role






To support and assist the Service Medical Director and Heads of Units, Anaesthesia in the provision of high quality anaesthetic services across Monash health sites, consistent with Monash Health values.









Provide clinical leadership through active involvement in patient care.












Be available to medical colleagues for consultation and liaison as appropriate regarding patient care.












Support academic, research, education, training & supervision (both undergraduate and postgraduate) roles in the Department of Anaesthesia and Perioperative Medicine, Monash Health.












Contribute to the professional and corporate life in Victoria's largest public health service by participation in appropriate committees and educational platforms.












Contribute to ongoing service improvement and clinical and workforce innovation to ensure Monash Health provides high quality accessible anaesthetic services















What we offer:









Salary packaging












Onsite discounted staff parking












Discounted banking (BankVic)












Onsite Gym












Access to professional development courses and seminars











About You






What you need:









Specialist registration with the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA)












Fellowship of the Australian & New Zealand College of Anaesthetists.












Experience in clinical quality assurance and improvement process is required.












For full Paediatric scope of practice recognition, a 12 month fellowship, in a recognised tertiary Paediatric hospital, is required












A valid Employee Victorian Working with Children Check (WWCC) is required for all medical staff at Monash Health.












A minimum of a 12-month fellowship in a recognised tertiary cardiac centre hospital is required












A recognised qualification and or experience consistent with ANZCA professional document PG46 related to perioperative transoesophageal echocardiography: 





An Australian or New Zealand university qualification in echocardiography at diploma level or equivalent, or 






A pass in a board examination in echocardiography from the US National Board of Echocardiography (Examination of Special Competence in Adult Echocardiography, Examination of Special Competence in Advanced Perioperative Transesophageal Echocardiography), or equivalent, or 






A pass in an examination in echocardiography from the British Society of Echocardiography and Association of Cardiothoracic Anaesthetists or the European Association of Echocardiography and European Association of Cardiothoracic Anaesthesiologists, or equivalent, or 






A diploma in diagnostic ultrasound focused on echocardiography from the Australasian Society for Ultrasound in Medicine, or equivalent, or 






A fellowship in echocardiography of at least 12 months duration, or 






Possess the necessary cumulative experience before the ratification of ANZCA PG 46










For a confidential discussion and to explore this opportunity further, please reach out to Dr Robert Marr, Service Program Medical Director of Anaesthetics and Perioperative Medicine by email at Robert.Marr@monashhealth.org.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Monash Health exists to reimagine care, so that people can live their best lives. 






We provide safe and equitable care, for every stage of life, delivered with world-leading expertise and over 175 years of experience. 






As a leading academic health service, we're committed to providing tomorrow's care today by integrating research, teaching and training into everyday practice. 






Our team of 24,000 people are full hearted, open minded and all in. Together, we provide more than 250 integrated services for every stage of life at over 50 locations and in the community across south-east Melbourne, Victoria, serving 1.2 million residents in the South Metro Local Health Service Network. 


Are you currently part of the team at Monash Health? Use your network login to access the Monash Health Careers portal and discover all the job opportunities open to you, to support growing your career within the organisation.




To see first-hand what our colleagues think about working here, take a look at the following short videos monashhealth.org-careers.




About the Department - Program 


Join Monash Health as a Quality Systems & Insights Analyst and play a key role in improving the safety and quality of care for one of Victoria's largest health services. Combining data analytics, quality systems expertise and clinical governance insight, you'll transform information into meaningful action, support organisation wide quality systems, and help leaders make decisions that improve patient outcomes. If you enjoy solving problems, working with data, optimising systems, and partnering with stakeholders to drive continuous improvement and positive change, this is an opportunity to make a real impact across a complex and dynamic healthcare environment.


The Quality & Clinical Governance Unit plays a central role in supporting Monash Health's commitment to delivering safe, effective and high-quality care. The team provides leadership, systems and oversight that strengthen clinical governance, quality improvement, patient safety and organisational learning across the health service.


The Quality Insights & Systems team manages and optimises key quality systems, supports the collection and analysis of clinical governance information, and provides meaningful insights that help leaders identify risks, monitor performance and drive continuous improvement. Working collaboratively with programs and services across Monash Health, the team supports evidence-based decision-making and initiatives that enhance patient outcomes and organisational performance.







About the Role 








This is a part time ongoing position located at Monash Medical Centre, Clayton, you will work under the leadership of the Quality Insights & Systems manager and collaborate closely with the broader Quality & Clinical Governance team and stakeholders across Monash Health.


This is an exciting opportunity for a quality systems and data professional who enjoys combining analytical thinking, systems administration and continuous improvement to support safer patient care. The role is responsible for maintaining and optimising key organisational quality systems while developing meaningful clinical governance insights that inform decision-making and improvement initiatives.










Key responsibilities include:



Administering and optimising Monash Health's quality systems, including incident management, document control and audit platforms.


Analysing clinical quality data and other information sources to identify trends, risks and opportunities for improvement. 


Developing and delivering clinical governance reports, dashboards and insights that support leaders and teams. 


Providing user support, education and training to improve staff capability in quality systems and data interpretation. 


Working with internal stakeholders, external vendors and partner teams to enhance system performance, data integrity and governance processes. 


Contributing to quality improvement initiatives, system enhancements and process optimisation projects.









This role will involve working with stakeholders across multiple Monash Health sites. A hybrid working arrangement may be available in line with team and organisational requirements.







About You 


To be successful in this healthcare role, you will bring demonstrated experience in systems administration, data analysis and quality improvement within a complex organisational environment. 


You will be someone who is curious, analytical and solutions-focused, with the ability to translate data into meaningful insights and build strong collaborative relationships with a wide range of stakeholders.


You will have:




Experience administering, supporting or improving systems and processes in a complex organisation. 


Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret data, identify trends and communicate actionable insights. 


Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including report writing, presentations and development of guidance materials.


Strong stakeholder engagement and relationship-building capabilities. 


Experience providing education, training and support to end-users.


High attention to detail and a commitment to maintaining data integrity and quality. 


Demonstrated problem-solving skills and a continuous improvement mindset. 


Advanced Microsoft Office skills, particularly Excel.


Experience using RiskMan, PROMPT, MARS or similar systems will be highly regarded.



Mandatory Requirements:




Degree qualification in health, quality, business management, data analytics or a related discipline.


Current right to work in Australia. 


Ability to obtain and maintain required screening checks, including National Police Check and Working with Children Check.


Current Victorian Driver's Licence is highly desirable



 
Desirable:




Knowledge of quality, safety and clinical governance principles within a health service environment. 


Experience working in a complex healthcare organisation.This role offers the opportunity to contribute directly to Monash Health's quality and safety agenda, helping to strengthen systems, generate valuable organisational insights and support continuous improvement across one of Australia's largest health services.

Monash Health is the largest healthcare provider in Victoria and is recognised for its exceptional clinical care and research. We are dedicated to providing outstanding patient care. We appreciate our unique and vital role as an integral part of the communities we serve and the importance of maintaining our services in a changing environment. The integrity of our corporate systems is critical to our ability to deliver excellent care to every patient, every time.


This role represents an exciting opportunity within our Applications and Enablement team. Reporting to the Manager Finance Systems, you will play a key role in providing day-to-day functional support for Monash Health's Oracle Fusion applications. You will help ensure our systems operate reliably and efficiently while supporting Finance, Supply Chain, People & Culture and Payroll functions across the organisation. 


Working closely with business stakeholders, vendors and internal digital teams, you will contribute to resolving system issues, supporting business improvements, delivering user training and ensuring the ongoing success of our Oracle Fusion platform. 


If appointed, your contribution will be assessed across five Key Result Areas:




Application Support and Operation


Customer Service and Stakeholder Engagement


Training, Capability Uplift and Knowledge Enablement


Continuous Improvement and Change Support


System Integrity and Service Excellence 



This role is expected to work in a hybrid model, with a minimum of three days per week on site in our Scoresby Office.



About You


The Oracle Fusion Support Officer ensures the effective support and optimisation of Oracle Fusion applications across Monash Health. You are passionate about customer service and enjoy helping users resolve issues, improve processes and gain confidence using enterprise systems.


With strong communication skills and an ability to build positive stakeholder relationships, you can translate business needs into clearly articulated system issues, support requests or improvement opportunities. You are comfortable working with both technical teams and business users and thrive in a fast-paced environment where priorities can change quickly. 


Naturally curious and solution-focused, you enjoy troubleshooting issues, identifying trends and contributing to continuous improvement initiatives. You take pride in delivering high-quality support and maintaining strong working relationships across the organisation.


On a personal level, you are:




Highly organised and customer focused


Flexible and able to adapt readily to changing priorities


A highly effective communicator with strong stakeholder engagement skills


Analytical with strong problem-solving abilities


Committed to continuous learning and professional development


A collaborative team player who enjoys helping others succeed




What You Need


To be considered for this role, you will need to demonstrate:




Experience supporting enterprise business applications within a complex environment


Exposure to Oracle Fusion or similar applications and associated business processes


Experience managing incidents and service requests through a structured service management framework


Proven ability to investigate issues, identify root causes and coordinate resolution activities


Strong customer service and stakeholder management experience


Experience supporting testing activities, including User Acceptance Testing (UAT) and regression testing


Ability to develop and maintain user documentation, knowledge articles and training materials


Excellent written and verbal communication skills. 




While not mandatory requirements, experience with the following will be highly regarded:




Oracle Fusion ERP, SCM, HCM or Payroll modules or similar applications


Experience supporting payroll, finance or procurement systems


Experience working within a large public sector, healthcare or enterprise environment. 



We are especially interested in hearing from candidates who enjoy working in highly collaborative environments and have a passion for improving user experiences through technology.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Monash Health exists to reimagine care, so that people can live their best lives. 






We provide safe and equitable care, for every stage of life, delivered with world-leading expertise and over 175 years of experience. 






As a leading academic health service, we're committed to providing tomorrow's care today by integrating research, teaching and training into everyday practice. 






Our team of 24,000 people are full hearted, open minded and all in. Together, we provide more than 250 integrated services for every stage of life at over 50 locations and in the community across south-east Melbourne, Victoria, serving 1.2 million residents in the South Metro Local Health Service Network. 


Are you currently part of the team at Monash Health? Use your network login to access the Monash Health Careers portal and discover all the job opportunities open to you, to support growing your career within the organisation.




To see first-hand what our colleagues think about working here, take a look at the following short videos monashhealth.org-careers.

Shape how digital change is experienced across one of Australia's largest health services.



About the Service


The Design and Architecture Services Department provides strategic architectural leadership across Monash Health, ensuring digital investments, systems and solutions align with organisational priorities and deliver long-term value. Working closely with clinical, operational and technology stakeholders, the team guides technology strategy, solution design, portfolio management and architectural governance to create a connected, sustainable and future-ready digital ecosystem that supports exceptional patient care and service delivery.



About The Role


If appointed to this business-critical role, you'll provide strategic leadership across enterprise architecture, technology governance, solution design and application portfolio management. 


Leading a team of architects and technical specialists, and reporting to the Director, Digital Applications and Architecture, you'll be responsible for defining the future-state architecture for one of Australia's largest and most complex health services, ensuring digital investments align with clinical, operational and organisational priorities. Working closely with executive leaders, clinicians, technology teams and external partners, you'll establish architecture standards, guide major technology decisions and shape a connected, sustainable and future-ready digital ecosystem.


Success in the role will be measured across four key areas: 



Development and delivery of Monash Health's future-state architecture and technology roadmaps


Establishment of architecture governance, standards and design assurance practices


Application portfolio management, rationalisation and lifecycle planning 


Excellence in stakeholder engagement and development of trusted partnerships across clinical, operational and digital teams



This is a Full Time, ongoing role, based in our hybrid workplace. The importance of connection and relationship development across the business cannot be underestimated and you'll happily work on a Monash Health site at least half of your working week to support your team and drive this important work. Travel across Monash Health sites will be required.



About You


You're a strategic technology leader who sees the bigger picture and brings others on the journey. You recognise that great architecture is about more than technology, it's about aligning digital investments with organisational priorities, enabling innovation, managing risk and creating sustainable foundations for the future.


Equally comfortable influencing executives, collaborating with clinicians and working alongside technical teams to solve complex challenges, you have a strong background in enterprise architecture, digital transformation and technology strategy. In addition, you bring proven ability to translate organisational objectives into pragmatic roadmaps, standards and governance frameworks that deliver measurable value.


An inspiring leader, you build trust readily, creating alignment across diverse stakeholder groups and developing high performing teams. Combining strategic thinking with practical delivery, you're passionate about designing technology ecosystems that improve outcomes for clinicians, consumers and the broader health service.


What you'll bring:



Significant leadership experience in enterprise architecture, technology strategy, solution architecture or digital transformation within a large, complex organisation


Strong understanding of modern architecture practices, including cloud platforms, integration patterns, APIs, data ecosystems security, risk and compliance


Demonstrated experience developing architecture roadmaps, governance frameworks, standards and design assurance practices that support strategic technology investment


Proven success leading high-performance specialist teams and navigating organisational change within complex or highly regulated environments


Exceptional communication, stakeholder engagement and influencing skills, with the ability to work effectively across executive, clinical, operational and technical environments



Tertiary qualifications in Information Technology, Computer Science, Digital Health or a related discipline will be highly regarded.



Why Join Design and Architecture Services at Monash Health


Take advantage of a rare opportunity to shape and influence enterprise-wide technology strategy, drive digital transformation and play a key role in enabling the delivery of safer, connected and more sustainable healthcare. Working at the intersection of clinical care, technology and innovation, you'll help create smarter digital solutions that improve patient outcomes and support the clinicians who deliver them every day




At Monash Health, you will:




Work within a values-driven, purpose-led organisation 


Be part of a connected network of clinical, academic and system leaders 


Help drive innovation, inclusion and better health outcomes





We offer:




The opportunity to make a real impact on patient experience


A supportive, collaborative team environment


Ongoing learning and development opportunities


The chance to be part of Victoria's largest public health service




For a confidential discussion and to explore this opportunity further, please reach out to Victoria Hornidge, Director, Digital Applications, on 0425 728 838



Position Description can be found here





Our Culture and Values 






At Monash Health, our people are at the heart of everything we do. Our culture is inclusive, supportive and future-focused, underpinned by clear values and a commitment to continuous improvement. 






Our teams play a critical role in bringing our new strategy to life, challenging traditional approaches, embracing innovation,
